content:
Minor style question that came up in review, which as far as I could see isn't in the style guide. Do we like (A)

let some x := x? |
  throwError "no x"

or (B)

let some x := x?
  | throwError "no x"

?

I always figured | was meant to look like a match alt and therefore went with B, but you do save an indent if you use A.
The pretty-printer seems to say A, but as far as I can tell this is "an accident" in that there are no pretty-printing directives in the parser.

I don't believe this is a question that has been decided? Personally, I like B, but I do believe we also allow this to be a one-liner, which I think contradicts the "match alt" hypothesis. If people like B enough, I'd be ok with un-one-lining though
Though, don't we also allow match e with | ... => ... as a one-liner, it's just that these are rare in practice?
I do think they are discouraged at least?

I prefer (A) with the argument that it makes it "feel like"

unless let some x := x? do
  -- ...

i.e. like any other control flow operation. Also (B) looks weird with multiple lines and if we are supposed to see it as a match alt are we supposed to write it like this?

let some x := x?
  | -- think _ =>
    do1
    do2

I figure it would be

let some x := x?
  | do1
    do2

where you're still suggesting the match alt, but abbreviating the line that you're excluding from the match alt in that abbreviation
this thread seems like a better fit for #lean4 to me
Hmm, but I am asking about the mathlib style guide & conventions here
(Core seems not to care judging by source code, for what it's worth, but core also allows many other style violations that mathlib disallows...)

Robin Arnez said:

I prefer (A) with the argument that it makes it "feel like"

unless let some x := x? do
  -- ...

i.e. like any other control flow operation.

I like the control flow vibe in principle, but it's just kind of weird to me to have | (1) be the only non-wordlike version of that pattern (vs. do, else, arguably with) (2) already be used to prefix match alts with very similar circumstances/meaning, but not here.

My inclination for questions like this at the moment is:

try not to care too much, Marc will make sensible choices as he is writing the newer formatter, and after that is available we can mostly just say "let the formatter do its thing"

(I'm not suggesting that we won't be able to ask for changes, or change, the formatter Marc delivers. Just that consistency, and deferring to Marc's good opinions, are both very useful things. :-)
Is there any timeline for the formatter that you can share, or a guesstimated version it'll be available in? :fingers_crossed:
